metadata.title: Comprehensive Ancient World Genealogy Database — Phase 1
scope: Extra-Biblical (Book of Jubilees, 1 Enoch, Book of Jasher, Qumran Book of Giants)
Mesopotamian (Sumerian King List, Atrahasis, Epic of Gilgamesh, Enuma Elish, Berossus)
Arabian / Early Islamic (Adnanite & Qahtanite Chronicles, al-Tabari)
Vedic & Puranic Indian (Rigveda, Shatapatha Brahmana, Mahabharata, Ramayana, Vishnu Purana)
Ancient Chinese (Shiji, Shan Hai Jing, Bamboo Annals, Shangshu)
Ancient Japanese & Korean (Kojiki, Nihon Shoki, Samguk Yusa)
Eurasian Steppe / Turko-Mongol (Shiji Ch. 110, Oghuzname, Jami al-Tawarikh)

linkTypes.direct: Explicit parent-child or biological descent within primary canonical/ancient texts
linkTypes.expansion: Matriarchs, intermediate generations, or migrations supplied by extra-biblical or secondary ancient chronicles (Jubilees, 1 Enoch, Jasher, Puranas, Shiji)
linkTypes.cognate: Linguistically or historically attested cross-tradition identity/ethnonym bridge (e.g., Vedic Vivasvan = Avestan Vivanghant; Biblical Madai = Medes; Biblical Mizraim = Phoenician Misor/Egypt)
linkTypes.parallel: Independent structural/archetypal parallel across ancient corpora (e.g., Great Flood survivors, 10 antediluvian patriarchs/kings, tripartite world division)
linkTypes.syncretic: Classical or medieval chronicler synthesis grafting distant nations onto a single universal tree (e.g., Rashid al-Din linking Japheth to Oghuz Khan; Jasher linking Esau's grandson Zepho to Rome)

nodes.name: Primordial Human Ancestors
nodes.role: Comparative Convergence Node
nodes.notes: Structural convergence hub linking the primordial first humans across Near Eastern, Indo-Iranian, and East Asian traditions.

nodes.name: Great Flood / Cataclysm Survivors
nodes.role: Comparative Convergence Node
nodes.notes: Global ancestral bottleneck motif: a righteous survivor preserves humanity and restarts the post-cataclysm lineages of the earth.

nodes.name: Post-Flood Division of Nations
nodes.role: Comparative Convergence Node
nodes.notes: Comparative hub connecting the major ancient genealogical maps explaining how humanity branched into distinct nations across Eurasia and Africa.

nodes.name: Adam & Eve (Hawwah)
altNames: First Man & Mother of All Living
nodes.role: Primeval Progenitors
nodes.notes: Progenitors of humanity in Biblical and extra-biblical traditions. Jubilees 4 explicitly names their daughters Awan (wife of Cain) and Azura (wife of Seth).

nodes.name: Cain (Qayin) & Awan
nodes.role: Firstborn / Builder of City of Enoch
nodes.notes: Founder of the Cainite branch. Jubilees 4:9 identifies his wife as his sister Awan; Genesis 4 traces urbanization, metallurgy, and music through his line.

nodes.name: Lamech (Cainite) & Adah / Zillah
nodes.role: Patriarch of Crafts & Arts
nodes.notes: Descended via Cain -> Enoch -> Irad -> Mehujael -> Methushael -> Lamech. Father of Jabal (nomadic herders), Jubal (musicians), Tubal-cain (bronze/iron smiths), and Naamah (identified in Jasher 5:15 and Genesis Rabbah as Noah's wife).

nodes.name: Seth (Shet) & Azura
nodes.role: Patriarch of the Sethite Line
nodes.notes: Appointed in place of Abel. Jubilees 4:11 names his wife Azura. Josephus (Ant. 1.2.3) credits Seth's descendants with inventing astronomy and inscribing wisdom on two pillars to survive flood and fire.

nodes.name: Enosh -> Kenan -> Mahalalel
nodes.role: Antediluvian Patriarchs
nodes.notes: Jubilees supplies their wives: Noam (wife of Enosh), Mualeleth (wife of Kenan), and Dinah daughter of Barakiel (wife of Mahalalel).

nodes.name: Jared (Yered) & Baraka
nodes.role: Patriarch during the Descent of the Watchers
nodes.notes: 1 Enoch 6 and Jubilees 4:15 link his name ('descent') to the descent of the Watchers (Grigori) onto Mount Hermon.

nodes.name: The Watchers (Semyaza / Azazel) -> Nephilim
nodes.role: Extra-Biblical Mythic Intermarriage Lineage
nodes.notes: Extra-biblical traditions describe 200 Watchers taking human wives and siring the Nephilim/Giants (named Ohya, Hahya, and Mahaway in Qumran fragments), precipitating the Flood.

nodes.name: Enoch (Khanokh) & Edni
nodes.role: 7th Patriarch / Scribe of Righteousness
nodes.notes: 7th from Adam; lived 365 years (solar cycle) and 'walked with God' without dying. Jubilees 4:17 credits him as the first human to learn writing, calendar, and astronomy. Strongly compared by Assyriologists to Enmeduranki, 7th antediluvian king of Sippar.

nodes.name: Methuselah & Lamech (Sethite)
nodes.role: Custodians of Enoch's Lore
nodes.notes: Jubilees names their wives Edna and Betenos. 1 Enoch 106 and the Dead Sea Scroll Genesis Apocryphon recount Lamech consulting Methuselah and Enoch over Noah's radiant, angelic birth.

nodes.name: Noah (Noach) & Emzara / Naamah
nodes.role: Great Flood Survivor / Universal Post-Flood Ancestor
nodes.notes: 10th from Adam. Jubilees 4:33 names his wife Emzara; Jasher 5:15 names her Naamah (daughter of Enoch or Lamech). All post-Flood nations in Genesis 10 descend from his three sons.

nodes.name: Shem (Sem) & Sedeqetelebab
nodes.role: Progenitor of Near Eastern & Semitic Nations
nodes.notes: Assigned the central temperate zone of Asia (from the Mediterranean to India/Tinas) in Jubilees 8. Father of Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.

nodes.name: Ham (Cham) & Na'eltama'uk
nodes.role: Progenitor of Cush, Mizraim, Phut, Canaan
nodes.notes: Assigned the southern zone (Africa and parts of Arabia/Levant) in Jubilees 8. Father of Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan.

nodes.name: Japheth (Yefet) & Adataneses
nodes.role: Progenitor of Northern Eurasian & Mediterranean Peoples
nodes.notes: Assigned the northern lands (Anatolia, Europe, Iranian Plateau, Eurasian Steppe) in Jubilees 8. Father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

nodes.name: Elam, Asshur, Lud & Aram
nodes.role: Eponymous Founders of Ancient Near Eastern Kingdoms
nodes.notes: Directly bridge Biblical genealogy to historical kingdoms: Elam (SW Iran/Susa), Asshur (Assyria/Ashur), Lud (Lydia in Anatolia), and Aram (Syria/Arameans).

nodes.name: Arphaxad -> (Cainan) -> Salah -> Eber
nodes.role: Eponym of the Hebrews ('Ivrim) & Southern Arabs
nodes.notes: Jubilees 8:1-4 (and the Septuagint) inserts Cainan son of Arphaxad, who discovers a rock inscription of the Watchers' astrological teachings. Eber's two sons, Peleg and Joktan, split the line into Mesopotamian-Levantine Hebrews and Arabian Qahtanites.

nodes.name: Peleg -> Reu -> Serug -> Nahor -> Terah
nodes.role: Tower of Babel Era to Ur of the Chaldees
nodes.notes: Peleg's name marks the 'division' of the earth (Tower of Babel). Jasher 7-11 depicts Terah as a military commander under Nimrod in Shinar before Abraham breaks his idols and migrates from Ur to Haran.

nodes.name: Abraham (Abram) & Sarah / Hagar / Keturah
nodes.role: Common Patriarch of Israelites, Ishmaelites, Edomites, Midianites
nodes.notes: Major convergence node for Abrahamic traditions: father of Isaac (via Sarah), Ishmael (via Hagar), and six Arabian/Transjordanian tribes including Midian (via Keturah); uncle of Lot (ancestor of Moab & Ammon).

nodes.name: Isaac -> Jacob (Israel) -> 12 Tribes of Israel
nodes.role: Israelite Patriarchal & Royal Lineage
nodes.notes: Branches into Levi (-> Moses & Aaron), Judah (-> Perez -> Boaz -> Jesse -> King David -> Solomon), Joseph (-> Ephraim & Manasseh), and the remaining tribes.

nodes.name: Esau (Edom) -> Eliphaz -> Zepho
nodes.role: Progenitor of Edom & Traditional Jasher Bridge to Italy/Rome
nodes.notes: Genesis 36 records Esau's line in Seir/Edom. The Book of Jasher (ch. 57, 61) famously narrates Esau's grandson Zepho fleeing Egypt to Kittim (Italy) and becoming king there—a traditional midrashic bridge linking Edom to Rome.

nodes.name: Midian & Keturah's Sons
altNames: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah
nodes.role: NW Arabian & Sinai Lineages
nodes.notes: Connects Abraham to the Midianites of NW Arabia/Sinai, including Jethro (Reuel/Shu'ayb) and Zipporah (wife of Moses).

nodes.name: Cush -> Nimrod (Mighty Hunter of Shinar)
nodes.role: Builder of Babel, Erech (Uruk), Accad, Nineveh
nodes.notes: Crucial Biblical-Mesopotamian bridge: Genesis 10:10-11 explicitly links Nimrod to Shinar (Sumer), Babel (Babylon), Erech (Uruk), Accad (Akkad), and Nineveh. Jasher 7 claims Nimrod wore Adam's garments and ruled the world at Babel.

nodes.name: Mizraim, Phut & Canaan
nodes.role: Eponyms of Egypt, North Africa, & Levantine Peoples
nodes.notes: Mizraim is the Hebrew/Semitic name for Egypt (and cognate with Phoenician Misor). Canaan fathers Sidon, Heth (Hittites), Amorites, and Sinites (later speculated by early modern writers to be China, though geographically coastal Phoenicia).

nodes.name: Gomer, Magog, Tubal, Meshech & Tiras
nodes.role: Anatolian, Pontic Steppe, & Northern Eurasian Peoples
nodes.notes: Gomer (Assyrian Gimirrai / Cimmerians) fathers Ashkenaz (Ashkuza / Scythians), Riphath, and Togarmah (Armenia/Anatolia). Magog becomes the medieval chronicler anchor for Steppe, Turkic, and Eurasian peoples.

nodes.name: Madai (Medes)
nodes.role: Biblical Bridge to the Iranian Plateau
nodes.notes: Direct historical/linguistic cognate with the Iranian Medes (Old Persian Mada). Jubilees 10:35 explains why Madai moved east into the Iranian highlands near Shem's territory (marrying a daughter of Shem).

nodes.name: Javan (Ionians / Greeks)
nodes.role: Biblical Bridge to the Aegean & Mediterranean
nodes.notes: Linguistic cognate of Ionia (Greek Iawones). His sons map to Cyprus (Kittim), Rhodes (Rodanim/Dodanim), Alashiya/Cyprus (Elishah), and Tarshish (Tartessos/Cilicia).

nodes.name: Apsu & Tiamat -> Anu -> Enki (Ea) -> Marduk
nodes.role: Creators of Humanity (Lullu from Qingu / We-ilu)
nodes.notes: In Atrahasis and Enuma Elish, Enki (Ea) and Nintu/Belet-ili fashion the first humans (Lullu) from clay mixed with divine blood, paralleling Adam's creation from dust/adamah.

nodes.name: Alulim of Eridu -> Antediluvian Kings (1-6)
nodes.role: First Kings When Kingship Descended from Heaven
nodes.notes: 8 kings in the Weld-Blundell Prism (10 in Berossus's Babylonian list), reigning immense ages before the Flood—closely mirroring the 10 long-lived antediluvian patriarchs of Genesis 5.

nodes.name: En-men-dur-ana (Enmeduranki) of Sippar
nodes.role: 7th King / Initiated into Heavenly Secrets by Shamash
nodes.notes: 7th antediluvian king in Berossus/Nippur traditions, ruler of Sippar (city of sun god Shamash), taken into the divine assembly to learn oil/liver divination and celestial tablets—widely recognized by scholars as a direct structural parallel to Enoch (7th patriarch, 365 solar years).

nodes.name: Ubara-Tutu -> Ziusudra / Utnapishtim / Atrahasis
nodes.role: Mesopotamian Great Flood Survivor
nodes.notes: Warned by Enki/Ea of the impending Deluge, builds a reed-and-timber vessel preserving family and animals, sends out dove/swallow/raven, and offers sacrifice upon landing (Mt. Nimush).

nodes.name: Meskiaggasher -> Enmerkar -> Lugalbanda -> Gilgamesh
nodes.role: Hero-Kings of Uruk (Biblical Erech)
sources: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta
nodes.notes: Gilgamesh (son of King Lugalbanda and goddess Ninsun) journeys to meet his ancestor/elder Utnapishtim to learn the secret of the Flood. Uruk is explicitly named 'Erech' in Genesis 10:10.

nodes.name: Sargon of Akkad -> Enheduanna & Naram-Sin
nodes.role: First Imperial Dynasty of Mesopotamia
nodes.notes: Founder of the Akkadian Empire (Biblical 'Accad' in Gen 10:10). His daughter Enheduanna is the earliest named author in world history. Often compared by historians to the memory of Nimrod (alongside Tukulti-Ninurta I and Ninurta).

nodes.name: Gayomart (Keyumars) -> Mashya & Mashyana
nodes.role: First Mortal & Primeval Iranian Couple
nodes.notes: Created by Ahura Mazda. From Gayomart's seed grew a rhubarb plant splitting into Mashya and Mashyana, the first human couple who bore 7 pairs of twins populating the 7 climes (karshvars) of the world.

nodes.name: Hushang -> Tahmuras -> Vivanghant (Vivanhao)
nodes.role: Father of Yima / Proto-Indo-Iranian Lineage Anchor
nodes.notes: EXACT Proto-Indo-Iranian linguistic & genealogical cognate of Vedic Vivasvan (Surya)! One of the strongest academically verified prehistoric genealogical bridges between Iran and India.

nodes.name: Yima Khshaeta (Jamshid)
nodes.role: Golden Age King & Cataclysm Ark (Vara) Builder
nodes.notes: Son of Vivanghant—direct Proto-Indo-Iranian cognate of Vedic Yama (son of Vivasvan). Warned by Ahura Mazda of a world-destroying catastrophic winter/meltwater flood (Mahrkusha), Yima builds the subterranean Vara preserving pairs of humans, animals, and plants.

nodes.name: Fereydun (Thraetaona)
nodes.role: Divider of the World Among Three Sons
nodes.notes: Descendant of Yima's line (son of Abtin/Athwya). Divides the entire known earth into three realms among his three sons—a striking tripartite parallel to Noah's division among Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

nodes.name: Salm (West/Rum), Tur (Turan/Steppe) & Iraj (Iran)
nodes.role: Eponymous Ancestors of Western, Steppe, and Iranian Peoples
nodes.notes: Salm receives the West (Anatolia/Rome), Tur receives Central Asia/Turan (Steppe & China borderlands), and Iraj receives Iran (Eranshahr). Iraj's descendants form the Kayanian royal dynasty (Manuchehr -> Kay Kavad -> Kay Kavus -> Siyavash -> Kay Khosrow).

nodes.name: Medes (Deioces / Cyaxares) & Achaemenids (Cyrus the Great)
nodes.role: Historical Iranian Empires
nodes.notes: Historical Iranian dynasties linking directly to Biblical Madai (Medes) and Elam (Cyrus was King of Anshan in Elam!).

nodes.name: Atum -> Shu/Tefnut -> Geb/Nut -> Osiris & Isis -> Horus
nodes.role: Divine Ancestral Genealogy of Egyptian Pharaohs
nodes.notes: Egyptian royal lists (Turin Papyrus, Manetho) trace historical kingship directly from the Ennead and Horus through the Shemsu-Hor ('Followers of Horus') to Menes/Narmer (c. 3100 BCE).

nodes.name: Menes / Narmer -> Early Dynastic Pharaohs
nodes.role: First Historical King of Egypt (Mizraim)
nodes.notes: Historical anchor for the land of Mizraim (Egypt). In medieval Coptic/Arabic lore (e.g., Murtada / al-Maqrizi), Misrayim/Misr is syncretically placed at the head of Egypt's post-Flood kings.

nodes.name: Protogonos -> Misor & Sydyk -> Taaut (Thoth) & Canaan
nodes.era: Bronze/Iron Age Levantine Lore (preserved 1st-2nd c. CE)
nodes.role: Phoenician-Canaanite Genealogy Bridging Egypt & Levant
sources: Eusebius Praeparatio Evangelica I.10 (quoting Philo of Byblos / Sanchuniathon)
nodes.notes: Explicitly names Misor (direct cognate of Biblical Mizraim!) as brother of Sydyk (Righteousness, cf. Melchizedek!) and father of Taaut (Egyptian Thoth, inventor of the alphabet), alongside Chna (Canaan).

nodes.name: Joktan (Qahtan) -> Ya'rub -> Saba (Sheba) -> Himyar & Kahlan
nodes.role: Ancestral Lineage of Yemen & Southern Arabia
nodes.notes: Arabian genealogical tradition identifies Qahtan with Biblical Joktan son of Eber (Prophet Hud), father of Sabaean (Sheba), Himyarite, and Kahlanite lineages.

nodes.name: Ishmael (Isma'il) -> Kedar/Nebaioth -> Adnan -> Quraysh
nodes.role: Northern Arabian & Prophetic Lineage
nodes.notes: Ishmael's sons Nebaioth and Kedar are corroborated as North Arabian tribes (Nabayati, Qidri) in Neo-Assyrian inscriptions. Classical Arab genealogists trace Adnan -> Ma'add -> Nizar -> Mudar -> Quraysh -> Hashim -> Muhammad.

nodes.name: Brahma -> Svayambhuva Manu & Shatarupa
nodes.role: Vedic Primordial Ancestors & Mind-Born Sages
nodes.notes: Brahma divides his form into Svayambhuva Manu (first human progenitor) and Shatarupa, while also generating the Saptarishis (including Marichi and Atri) from whom both Solar and Lunar dynasties descend.

nodes.name: Marichi -> Kashyapa (+ Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru)
altNames: Father of Devas, Asuras, Nagas, & Humans
nodes.role: Universal Progenitor Sage (Prajapati)
nodes.notes: Through Daksha's daughters, Kashyapa fathers the Adityas (including Vivasvan/Surya via Aditi), Daityas, Danavas, Garudas, and Nagas—making him a foundational common ancestor in Hindu cosmology.

nodes.name: Vivasvan (Surya)
nodes.role: Father of Vaivasvata Manu & Yama (Indo-Iranian Bridge)
nodes.notes: Linguistically and genealogically identical to Avestan Vivanghant! Father of Yama (Avestan Yima/Jamshid) and Vaivasvata Manu (Great Flood survivor).

nodes.name: Yama & Yami
altNames: First Mortal to Pass to the Afterlife
nodes.role: Twin First Mortals / Exact Cognate of Avestan Yima
nodes.notes: Son of Vivasvan, exact cognate of Iranian Yima (Jamshid) son of Vivanghant—confirming a shared Proto-Indo-Iranian ancestral genealogy predating c. 2000 BCE.

nodes.name: Vaivasvata Manu (Shraddhadeva)
nodes.role: Vedic Great Flood Survivor (Saved by Matsya)
nodes.notes: Warned by a miraculous fish (Matsya, avatar of Vishnu) of the universal Deluge, builds a ship towed to the Northern Mountains (Himalayas). Through his son Ikshvaku and daughter/son Ila, he is the common ancestor of ALL humanity (Manava) in the current age.

nodes.name: Ikshvaku -> Raghu -> Dasharatha -> Rama (Surya Vamsha)
nodes.role: Solar Royal Dynasty (Ramayana & Shakya/Buddhist Lineage)
nodes.notes: Son of Vaivasvata Manu. Produces King Harishchandra, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Prince Rama. Crucially, Buddhist chronicles (Mahavamsa, Ambattha Sutta) trace the Shakya clan of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) to King Okkaka = Ikshvaku!

nodes.name: Atri -> Soma -> Budha + Ila (of Manu) -> Pururavas -> Yayati
nodes.role: Union of Solar & Lunar Lines / Father of the 5 Vedic Peoples
nodes.notes: Unites Rishi Atri's lunar line with Vaivasvata Manu's bloodline via Ila. Great-grandson Yayati fathers the five famous Vedic tribes (Panchajana) that serve as India's ancient 'Table of Nations'.

nodes.name: Yayati's 5 Sons: Yadu, Turvasu, Druhyu, Anu & Puru
nodes.role: Vedic Table of Nations (South & Central Asian Branches)
nodes.notes: Puranic ethnography assigns Yadu -> Yadavas (Krishna), Puru -> Bharatas/Kurus (Central India), Anu -> East/North (Anga, Vanga, Shibi), Turvasu -> South/West, and Druhyu -> Northwest (Gandhara and trans-Indus Mleccha/Central Asian tribes!).

nodes.name: Puru -> Bharata -> Kuru -> Pandavas & Kauravas (Mahabharata)
nodes.role: Eponym of India (Bharatavarsha) & Mahabharata Line
nodes.notes: Emperor Bharata gives India its classical name (Bharatavarsha). Descends via Kuru and Vyasa to the Pandavas (Arjuna -> Abhimanyu -> Parikshit) and interacts with their cousins the Yadavas (Krishna, from Yadu).

nodes.name: Fuxi & Nüwa (Three Sovereigns)
nodes.role: Primordial Sibling-Consorts / Clay-Creators & Flood Survivors
nodes.notes: Depicted with intertwined serpent tails holding compass and square. Nüwa repairs the shattered sky pillars after Gonggong's flood and molds humanity from yellow clay. Later folklore (and SW Chinese Miao/Yao traditions) preserves Fuxi & Nüwa as Great Flood survivors.

nodes.name: Yandi (Flame Emperor / Shennong)
nodes.role: Co-Progenitor of the Chinese People (Yan-Huang)
nodes.notes: Guoyu records Yandi (Jiang clan) and Huangdi (Ji clan) as half-brothers born of Shaodian! Their alliance after the Battle of Banquan creates the unified Huaxia ancestry ('Yan-Huang Zisun' — Descendants of Yan and Huang).

nodes.name: Huangdi (Yellow Emperor) & Leizu
nodes.role: Universal Royal Ancestor in Sima Qian's Shiji
sources: Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian) Ch. 1
nodes.notes: Sima Qian's Shiji (c. 94 BCE) systematically traces ALL Five Emperors AND all Three Ancient Dynasties (Xia, Shang, Zhou) AND the northern Xiongnu back to Huangdi's 25 sons (14 surnames)!

nodes.name: Changyi -> Zhuanxu (Gaoyang)
nodes.role: Ancestor of Xia Dynasty, Emperor Shun, & Chu/Qin States
nodes.notes: Grandson of Huangdi. Separates Heaven and Earth (ordering cosmic/human realms). Progenitor of Gun -> Yu the Great (Xia), Emperor Shun, the royal house of Chu, and the House of Ying (Qin Shi Huang!).

nodes.name: Gun -> Yu the Great (Da Yu) -> Qi (Xia Dynasty)
nodes.role: Chinese Great Flood Hero & First Hereditary Dynasty
nodes.notes: After his father Gun fails to dam the Great Flood (Gun-Yu Flood), Yu spends 13 years dredging channels to drain the waters into the sea, establishing the Nine Provinces and the Xia Dynasty.

nodes.name: Emperor Ku (Di Ku) -> Emperor Yao & Shun
nodes.role: Sage Emperors & Ancestor of Shang and Zhou Dynasties
nodes.notes: Descended from Huangdi via Xuanxiao -> Jiaoji -> Di Ku. Di Ku fathers Emperor Yao (who abdicates to Shun, a descendant of Zhuanxu), Xie (ancestor of Shang), and Hou Ji (ancestor of Zhou).

nodes.name: Xie (Shang Dynasty) & Hou Ji (Zhou Dynasty)
altNames: Zi Clan (Shang) & Ji Clan (Zhou -> Confucius/Duke of Zhou)
nodes.role: Historical Oracle-Bone & Classical Chinese Dynasties
nodes.notes: Shang Dynasty (verified by oracle bones at Anyang; Confucius later claimed descent from the Shang royal line via Song!). Zhou Dynasty (King Wen, King Wu, Duke of Zhou) descended from Hou Ji (Lord Millet).

nodes.name: Izanagi & Izanami -> Amaterasu & Susanoo
nodes.role: Japanese Primordial Couple & Sun Goddess
nodes.notes: Izanagi and Izanami stir the primeval ocean with the heavenly jeweled spear to birth the Japanese archipelago and the deities Amaterasu (Sun), Tsukuyomi (Moon), and Susanoo (Storm).

nodes.name: Ninigi-no-Mikoto -> Hoori -> Emperor Jimmu
nodes.role: Founder of Japan's Continuous Imperial Lineage
nodes.notes: Great-great-great-grandson of Amaterasu through Ninigi's descent to Mount Takachiho. Traditional founder of the Yamato Imperial Dynasty.

nodes.name: Hwanin -> Hwanung + Ungnyeo -> Dangun Wanggeom
nodes.role: Mythic Progenitor of the Korean People
sources: Samguk Yusa (1281 CE, citing lost Wei Shu / Gogi)
nodes.notes: Son of heavenly prince Hwanung and the bear-turned-woman Ungnyeo. Later Korean and Chinese annals (Shiji, Book of Han) also link the Shang prince Jizi (Gija) migrating to Joseon after 1046 BCE.

nodes.name: Chunwei -> Xiongnu (Modu Chanyu)
nodes.role: Sima Qian's Bridge Between Chinese Xia & Inner Asian Steppe
sources: Sima Qian Shiji Ch. 110 (Account of the Xiongnu)
nodes.notes: Sima Qian explicitly records that the ancestor of the Xiongnu was Chunwei, a descendant of the Xia Dynasty ruling house who moved north into the steppes—an ancient Chinese genealogical bridge into Eurasia.

nodes.name: Turk (Oljai Khan) -> Oghuz Khagan (6 Sons / 24 Tribes)
nodes.role: Eponymous Ancestor of Turkic Peoples (Bridged to Japheth & Turan)
nodes.notes: Medieval Eurasian historians (Rashid al-Din, Abulghazi) explicitly grafted Turkic and Mongol genealogies onto Biblical Japheth (Yafith -> Oljai Khan -> Tatar & Mongol -> Kara Khan -> Oghuz Khagan -> 6 sons: Gun, Ay, Yildiz, Gok, Dag, Deniz), creating a famous universal Eurasian tree.
